author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The confirmed death toll from a ferry fire in the Philippines rose to 76 on Saturday after responders recovered 41 additional charred remains, authorities said. Thirteen people were still unaccounted for, while 43 survivors had been confirmed from the vessel carrying more than 130 people.

Rescue teams entered the ferry on Friday after the fire was extinguished and found many of the remains in the economy passenger section. The Maritime Industry Authority said survivors reported hearing two explosions, but investigators have not established what started the blaze. Identification work is continuing alongside the search for those still missing.

The new toll is a substantial increase from earlier reports and may change again as recovery teams complete their work. Authorities are also reviewing the passenger count and the sequence of events aboard the vessel. The disaster has shifted from an active rescue toward recovery, identification and investigation, though families are still waiting for definitive information. Officials have not announced a final cause. Until the inquiry is complete, reports about explosions describe witness accounts rather than a determination of why the fire spread.
dek: Responders recovered 41 additional remains as identification work continued and 13 people remained unaccounted for.
headline: Philippine ferry-fire death toll rises to 76
